China convenes symposium to deepen media cooperation with regime November 19, 2026 China continued its push to shape narratives in Myanmar by convening regime-aligned media figures, officials and commentators in Yangon on Tuesday to promote President Xi Jinping’s four flagship global initiatives and deepen media cooperation with the junta. Speaking at a symposium on the initiatives and the fourth-quarter 2026 China-Myanmar Media Exchange, Chinese Ambassador Ma Jia highlighted growing bilateral cooperation in security, governance and people-to-people exchanges. She said China and Myanmar were deepening law-enforcement cooperation to combat cross-border crimes, including online scam operations and online gambling, while expanding cultural exchanges to strengthen mutual understanding between the two countries’ peoples. The event brought together staunch military supporters including Lower House MP Aye Chan, Myanmar Press Council chairman Dr. Tin Tun Oo, Myanmar Narrative Think Tank chairman Ko Ko, officials from the regime and regime-aligned media. Ma said Myanmar was cooperating with China through several governance-related mechanisms, including the Group of Friends of Global Governance and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. Aye Chan urged Beijing to place greater emphasis on small-scale projects that directly benefit local communities rather than focusing mainly on large infrastructure schemes. The proposal comes as several China-backed mega projects have stalled amid instability since the coup. The gathering follows a similar forum hosted by Ma in May, where she urged regime-linked media and opinion leaders to help promote favorable narratives about China-Myanmar cooperation. Regime spokeswoman Khaing Khaing Soe has said Myanmar is the only country to have formally signed on to all four of China’s Global Initiatives. (Photo: Chinese Embassy) #WhatsHappeningInMyanmar
